name: xpc_init
prose: Precondition: none; called once as the module init routine. Postcondition: it sets the device names of xpc_part and xpc_chan. If is_uv_system() is false it returns -ENODEV (nothing else done); otherwise it calls xpc_init_uv and returns its error if non-zero (no teardown). It calls xpc_setup_partitions; on failure it logs and returns that error after only calling xpc_exit_uv (for a UV system; partitions are not torn down). It registers the 'xpc' and 'xpc/hb' sysctl tables (their results are checked only at teardown), calls xpc_setup_rsvd_page, and on failure returns that error after unregistering both sysctl tables, calling xpc_teardown_partitions and xpc_exit_uv. It then registers the reboot and die notifiers; a failure of either only logs a warning and initialisation continues without that notifier registered. It starts the heartbeat-checker kthread: on failure it returns -EBUSY after xpc_teardown_rsvd_page, unregistering both notifiers and both sysctl tables, and xpc_teardown_partitions and xpc_exit_uv. It starts the discovery kthread: on failure it completes xpc_discovery_exited, calls xpc_do_exit(xpUnloading) (which performs the teardown) and returns -EBUSY. If everything succeeds it calls xpc_set_interface with XPC's connect, disconnect, send, send-notify, received and nasid functions and returns 0, leaving the partition structures, reserved page, sysctl tables, any successfully registered notifiers and both kthreads in place.
note: Reviewer 2 right and already in the old prose (setup_partitions failure only calls xpc_exit_uv via out_1, xpc_main.c:1201-1204, 1279-1281); reviewer 3 right: on success a notifier whose registration failed is not registered (1222-1229), the old prose said both notifiers remain registered; reviewer 1 right (setup_rsvd_page failure return, covered). xpc_init at 1182-1283.

name: xpc_kthread_start
prose: Precondition: args packs a valid partition id and channel number; this kthread holds one msgqueue reference on the channel and one reference on the partition, and has been counted in ch->kthreads_assigned. Postcondition: it always returns 0. If XPC_C_DISCONNECTING is not set on the channel at entry: under ch->lock, if XPC_C_CONNECTEDCALLOUT is not yet set it sets it, calls xpc_connected_callout with the lock dropped, then sets XPC_C_CONNECTEDCALLOUT_MADE, and if more than one payload is deliverable and the channel is still not disconnecting it activates additional kthreads for the surplus; if XPC_C_CONNECTEDCALLOUT was already set it does none of that (no callout and MADE is not set by this call); in both cases it then calls xpc_kthread_waitmsgs, which delivers messages or idles until the channel disconnects or the idle limit is reached. If XPC_C_DISCONNECTING was already set at entry neither the callout nor xpc_kthread_waitmsgs is run. In all cases, under ch->lock, if XPC_C_CONNECTEDCALLOUT_MADE is set and XPC_C_DISCONNECTINGCALLOUT is not, it sets XPC_C_DISCONNECTINGCALLOUT, calls xpc_disconnect_callout with xpDisconnecting with the lock dropped and sets XPC_C_DISCONNECTINGCALLOUT_MADE. It then decrements ch->kthreads_assigned and, only if that reaches 0, decrements part->nchannels_engaged; only if both reach 0 does it call indicate_partition_disengaged. Finally it drops the channel's msgqueue reference with xpc_msgqueue_deref and the partition reference with xpc_part_deref.
note: Reviewers right: the callout flags are not always set (skipped if already set or the channel is disconnecting), disengagement needs both counters to reach zero (the second decrement is short-circuited, xpc_main.c:736-737), and xpc_kthread_waitmsgs is inside the 'not disconnecting' block (688-719), so the old prose's claim that it runs for an already disconnecting channel was wrong. xpc_kthread_start at 671-748.

name: xpc_handle_activate_mq_msg_uv
prose: Precondition: part points to the xpc_partition of the sending partition, msg_hdr points to a received activate-message header, part_setup is nonzero exactly when partition setup has completed, and wakeup_hb_checker points to a valid int counter. Postcondition: the function always stores msg_hdr->act_state into part->sn.uv.remote_act_state and returns with none of the locks it takes held (xpc_activate_IRQ_rcvd_lock, part->chctl_lock and part->sn.uv.flags_lock are each taken and released); for XPC_ACTIVATE_MQ_MSG_ACTIVATE_REQ_UV it sets part->sn.uv.act_state_req to XPC_P_ASR_ACTIVATE_UV (incrementing xpc_activate_IRQ_rcvd only if act_state_req was 0, under xpc_activate_IRQ_rcvd_lock), stores msg->rp_gpa in part->remote_rp_pa, msg_hdr->rp_ts_jiffies in part->remote_rp_ts_jiffies and msg->heartbeat_gpa in part->sn.uv.heartbeat_gpa, and when msg->activate_gru_mq_desc_gpa differs from part->sn.uv.activate_gru_mq_desc_gpa clears XPC_P_CACHED_ACTIVATE_GRU_MQ_DESC_UV under part->sn.uv.flags_lock and stores the new value, then increments *wakeup_hb_checker; for XPC_ACTIVATE_MQ_MSG_DEACTIVATE_REQ_UV it sets part->sn.uv.act_state_req to XPC_P_ASR_DEACTIVATE_UV (incrementing xpc_activate_IRQ_rcvd only if act_state_req was 0), stores msg->reason in part->sn.uv.reason, increments *wakeup_hb_checker and returns immediately; for XPC_ACTIVATE_MQ_MSG_CHCTL_CLOSEREQUEST_UV, XPC_ACTIVATE_MQ_MSG_CHCTL_CLOSEREPLY_UV, XPC_ACTIVATE_MQ_MSG_CHCTL_OPENREQUEST_UV and XPC_ACTIVATE_MQ_MSG_CHCTL_OPENREPLY_UV it does nothing beyond the remote_act_state update when part_setup is 0, and when part_setup is nonzero it stores the message fields into part->remote_openclose_args[msg->ch_number] (reason for CLOSEREQUEST, entry_size and local_nentries for OPENREQUEST, remote_nentries, local_nentries and local_msgqueue_pa from notify_gru_mq_desc_gpa for OPENREPLY), sets the corresponding XPC_CHCTL_* bit in part->chctl.flags[msg->ch_number] under part->chctl_lock and calls xpc_wakeup_channel_mgr(part); for XPC_ACTIVATE_MQ_MSG_CHCTL_OPENCOMPLETE_UV with part_setup nonzero it sets XPC_CHCTL_OPENCOMPLETE in part->chctl.flags[msg->ch_number] under part->chctl_lock, calls xpc_wakeup_channel_mgr(part) and falls through to set XPC_P_ENGAGED_UV in part->sn.uv.flags under part->sn.uv.flags_lock, while with part_setup zero it breaks out at once without any channel handling and without setting XPC_P_ENGAGED_UV; for XPC_ACTIVATE_MQ_MSG_MARK_ENGAGED_UV it sets XPC_P_ENGAGED_UV in part->sn.uv.flags under part->sn.uv.flags_lock; for XPC_ACTIVATE_MQ_MSG_MARK_DISENGAGED_UV it clears XPC_P_ENGAGED_UV in part->sn.uv.flags under part->sn.uv.flags_lock; for XPC_ACTIVATE_MQ_MSG_SYNC_ACT_STATE_UV it only updates remote_act_state; for any other type it logs an error and sets part->sn.uv.act_state_req to XPC_P_ASR_DEACTIVATE_UV with part->sn.uv.reason = xpBadMsgType (incrementing xpc_activate_IRQ_rcvd only if act_state_req was 0, under xpc_activate_IRQ_rcvd_lock), increments *wakeup_hb_checker and returns immediately; finally, on every path that does not return early, if msg_hdr->rp_ts_jiffies differs from part->remote_rp_ts_jiffies and part->remote_rp_ts_jiffies is nonzero it sets part->sn.uv.act_state_req to XPC_P_ASR_REACTIVATE_UV (incrementing xpc_activate_IRQ_rcvd only if act_state_req was 0, under xpc_activate_IRQ_rcvd_lock) and increments *wakeup_hb_checker; the function has no return value and reports no error.
note: Reviewer 3 right: in the OPENCOMPLETE case 'if (!part_setup) break;' (xpc_uv.c:495-496) leaves the switch before the fallthrough to MARK_ENGAGED, so XPC_P_ENGAGED_UV is not set when part_setup is 0; the old prose said it still fell through. Every other branch re-checked against 351-549 (activate/deactivate requests, the four open/close channel messages, MARK_ENGAGED/DISENGAGED, SYNC, the default bad-message path, and the final REACTIVATE check); unchanged.

name: vmci_ctx_add_notification
prose: Precondition: context_id and remote_cid are u32 context ids. Postcondition: it returns VMCI_ERROR_NOT_FOUND (-21) if vmci_ctx_get finds no context with id context_id. Otherwise (the reference from vmci_ctx_get is released with vmci_ctx_put on every following path) it returns VMCI_ERROR_DST_UNREACHABLE (-10) if both context_id and remote_cid are VM contexts, VMCI_ERROR_NO_ACCESS (-7) if the context has VMCI_PRIVILEGE_FLAG_RESTRICTED set, and VMCI_ERROR_NO_MEM (-3) if the kmalloc of the list node fails. Otherwise it builds the handle vmci_make_handle(remote_cid, VMCI_EVENT_HANDLER) and, with context->lock held (spin_lock), returns VMCI_ERROR_NO_MEM (-3) after freeing the node if context->n_notifiers is already VMCI_MAX_CONTEXTS (2000), returns VMCI_ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS (-22) after freeing the node if an equal handle is already in the notifier list, and otherwise appends the node to context->notifier_list with list_add_tail_rcu, increments n_notifiers and returns VMCI_SUCCESS (0). The lock is released before the context reference is put, and on every failure path the notifier list and n_notifiers are unchanged and the temporary node is freed.
note: Old prose had wrong numeric error codes (-17 for NOT_FOUND, -18, -5, -4); all four reviewers' replacement numbers were also wrong. Actual values from vmw_vmci_defs.h:262-290: NO_MEM -3, NO_ACCESS -7, DST_UNREACHABLE -10, NOT_FOUND -21, ALREADY_EXISTS -22. So each reviewer was right that the codes were wrong and wrong about what they should be (reviewer 1 right on NO_ACCESS -7). Contract left empty. vmci_ctx_add_notification at 578-639.

name: vmci_ctx_remove_notification
prose: Precondition: context_id and remote_cid are u32 context ids. Postcondition: it returns VMCI_ERROR_NOT_FOUND (-21) if vmci_ctx_get finds no context with id context_id. Otherwise, with context->lock held (spin_lock), it searches context->notifier_list for an entry whose handle equals vmci_make_handle(remote_cid, VMCI_EVENT_HANDLER); if one is found it unlinks it with list_del_rcu and decrements n_notifiers. After releasing the lock it frees the found entry after an RCU grace period with kvfree_rcu_mightsleep (which may sleep). It then releases the context reference with vmci_ctx_put and returns VMCI_SUCCESS (0) if an entry was removed, or VMCI_ERROR_NOT_FOUND (-21) if none matched, in which case the list and n_notifiers are unchanged. No lock is held on return.
note: Old prose gave NOT_FOUND as -17; the real value is -21 (vmw_vmci_defs.h:288), and reviewers 1 (-9) and 3 (-11) were wrong too. The old prose said the entry was freed 'under' the lock-protected removal; the free via kvfree_rcu_mightsleep happens after the lock is released (669-670). vmci_ctx_remove_notification at 645-675.

name: check_status
prose: Precondition: rsp_sts is a u64 value read from the MIO_EMM_RSP_STS register. Postcondition: it returns -EILSEQ (-84) if any of the response-bad-status (bit 13), response-CRC-error (bit 14) or block-CRC-error (bit 21) bits is set; otherwise -ETIMEDOUT (-110) if the response-timeout (bit 15) or block-timeout (bit 22) bit is set; otherwise -EIO (-5) if the DBUF-error bit (bit 28) is set; otherwise 0. It reads no state, takes no locks and allocates nothing.
note: Old prose and contract used wrong bit numbers (23, 24, 27 and 25, 26): cavium.h:177-188 defines BAD_STS = bit 13, RSP_CRC_ERR = 14, RSP_TIMEOUT = 15, BLK_CRC_ERR = 21, BLK_TIMEOUT = 22, DBUF_ERR = 28, so the masks are 0x206000 (EILSEQ), 0x408000 (ETIMEDOUT) and 0x10000000 (EIO). Return order as in cavium.c:409-421. The earlier 'still-rejected' reasons were mechanical.

name: dw_mci_exynos_get_best_clksmpl
prose: Precondition: candidates is any 8-bit value (0..255); the function reads only its argument, takes no locks and acquires no references. Postcondition: it returns an s8 as follows. It returns the smallest i in 0..7 such that candidates rotated right by i bits within 8 bits (ror8) has bits 0, 1, 2, 6 and 7 all set (mask 0xc7); if there is no such i, it returns the smallest i in 0..7 whose rotation has bits 0, 1 and 7 all set (mask 0x83); if there is none, it returns the smallest i in 0..7 whose rotation has bit 0 set; if no rotation has bit 0 set (which happens only when candidates is 0), it returns -1.
note: Matches dw_mci_exynos_get_best_clksmpl (dw_mmc-exynos.c:495-531): three successive searches over i = 0..7 with masks 0xc7, 0x83 and 0x1, each returning the first match, otherwise -1. The old contract was removed: it was repeatedly rejected as unparsable (quantifiers, 'integer' variables) and I could not give a shorter exact one-line contract.

name: dw_mci_work_func
prose: Precondition: t is the bh_work work_struct embedded in a struct dw_mci (recovered with from_work); the caller does not hold host->lock (the function takes it). Postcondition: it takes host->lock with spin_lock, copies host->state, host->data and host->mrq into locals, and loops over the state machine (STATE_IDLE and STATE_WAITING_CMD11_DONE do nothing; SENDING_CMD11/SENDING_CMD, SENDING_DATA, DATA_BUSY, SENDING_STOP and DATA_ERROR each test and clear pending event bits, complete the command or data, stop DMA, send stop/abort commands, reset the controller or arm the data timeout with dw_mci_set_drto, and may move on to the next state) until a pass leaves the local state unchanged; then it stores that state in host->state and releases host->lock. Several paths instead leave through the unlock label without storing the local state: when the command was the set-block-count command (mrq->sbc) and completed without error it calls __dw_mci_start_request for mrq->cmd; and the paths that finish the request call dw_mci_request_end (after a command that has no data or failed, after data complete without a stop to send, after a data error with no command-complete pending, and in SENDING_STOP). dw_mci_request_end itself sets host->state (to STATE_IDLE, STATE_WAITING_CMD11_DONE or STATE_SENDING_CMD for a queued request), and it temporarily releases and retakes host->lock around mmc_request_done. The function returns nothing and releases host->lock before returning on every path.
note: Reviewer 1 right (the function takes host->lock itself); reviewer 2 right (the sbc path starts the next request and leaves without request_end or a state store, dw_mmc.c:2097-2100); reviewer 3 right (every request_end path goes to unlock without writing the local state to host->state: 2139, 2225, 2245, 2275, and request_end sets host->state itself, 1911-1919). The old prose treated the sbc path as the only exception. dw_mci_work_func at 2064-2291; request_end at 1894-1925.

name: mmci_probe
prose: Precondition: dev is an amba_device being probed and id->data points to a variant_data. Postcondition: it returns -EINVAL if there is neither platform data nor a device-tree node. If there is no platform data it allocates a zeroed one with devm_kzalloc (-ENOMEM on failure); it allocates the mmc host with devm_mmc_alloc_host (-ENOMEM), parses the DT with mmci_of_parse, for variants without an opendrain bit gets the pinctrl and its opendrain state, and gets the clock with devm_clk_get; each of these failures returns its error directly (nothing to undo but devm resources). It enables the clock with clk_prepare_enable (error returned directly) and from then on every failure path jumps to clk_disable, which calls clk_disable_unprepare on host->clk and returns the error: a clk_set_rate failure (when mclk exceeds the variant's maximum), a devm_ioremap_resource failure, a failure to get the optional reset control, a failure of mmc_regulator_get_supply, an -EPROBE_DEFER from mmc_gpiod_request_cd or mmc_gpiod_request_ro (looked up only when there is no DT node; any other error from those two calls is ignored), a failure to request the command IRQ (dev->irq[0]) or, if dev->irq[1] is present, the PIO IRQ, and a failure of mmc_add_host. A failure of reset_control_deassert is only logged. In between it sets host and mmc fields (clock limits, capabilities, busy detection, request size limits) and modifies the shared static mmci_ops (card_busy, enable_sdio_irq, ack_sdio_irq) when the variant supports those, programs the interrupt mask registers, sets the amba driver data, logs the device, calls mmci_dma_setup and configures autosuspend; the DMA setup, driver data and mmci_ops changes are not undone if mmc_add_host fails. On success it calls pm_runtime_put and returns 0 with the MMC host registered.
note: Reviewer right: mmc_gpiod_request_cd/ro errors other than -EPROBE_DEFER are not returned (mmci.c:2435-2443), the old prose listed them as returned errors. Slice cut the head: mmci_probe at 2203-2488 (name was right). Also added: shared static mmci_ops is modified (2357, 2371-2372) and mmci_dma_setup is not undone on a later failure.

name: msdc_drv_probe
prose: Precondition: pdev is a platform device bound to this driver, described by a device-tree node, with no per-device state set up yet. Postcondition: it returns -EINVAL if there is no DT node and -ENOMEM if devm_mmc_alloc_host fails; it then parses the MMC properties (mmc_of_parse), maps the registers (and the top registers if the match data needs them), gets the regulators, clocks (msdc_of_clock_parse), optional reset and, for eMMC, the optional crypto clock, the IRQ (platform_get_irq), the pinctrl handle and its default and uhs states, and optionally the SDIO wake-up interrupt and pinctrl state (a missing eint state is only logged); each failure in this stage returns its error directly (only devm resources, and possibly device_init_wakeup, were set up). It fills in the mmc parameters and allocates the two coherent DMA buffers (gpd and bd) without checking each separately; if either is NULL it returns -ENOMEM through release_mem, which disables wakeup and frees whichever buffer was allocated. It then initialises the descriptors, the work and the lock, sets the driver data and ungates the clocks; if msdc_ungate_clock fails it returns that error through release_clk, which gates the clocks, clears the driver data and runs release_mem (it does not call msdc_deinit_hw). It then calls msdc_init_hw, allocates and initialises the CQHCI host if the host has CQE support (-ENOMEM or the cqhci_init error), or otherwise, for hosts without SDIO support, a HSQ with mmc_hsq_init; failures of those, of devm_request_irq (error returned) go to release, which runs msdc_deinit_hw and then the release_clk and release_mem steps. It then sets up runtime PM with autosuspend and calls mmc_add_host; if that fails it disables runtime PM and runs the same unwind. On success it returns 0 with the host registered; resources owned by the device are released later by msdc_drv_remove.
note: Reviewer right: msdc_ungate_clock failure jumps to release_clk (mtk-sd.c:3108-3111), skipping msdc_deinit_hw, which the old prose said was run on every failure after platform_set_drvdata. Slice cut the head: msdc_drv_probe at 2960-3183 (name was right). Also pointed out the unchecked pair of DMA allocations (3093-3102).

name: omap_hsmmc_probe
prose: Precondition: pdev is a platform device bound to this driver; its platform data is pdev->dev.platform_data or, for an OF match, the data built by of_get_hsmmc_pdata. Postcondition: it returns PTR_ERR of of_get_hsmmc_pdata if that fails, -ENXIO if there is no platform data, the negative platform_get_irq result, the ioremap error, -ENOMEM if devm_mmc_alloc_host fails, the mmc_of_parse error, or the error of getting the 'fck' clock; each of these returns directly (nothing but devm resources acquired, though platform_set_drvdata may already have been called before the clock failure). It then sets the driver data and host fields, enables device wakeup and runtime PM, takes a runtime-PM reference with pm_runtime_get_sync, sets autosuspend, gets the optional 'mmchsdb_fck' debounce clock (host->dbclk is set to NULL if it is missing or if clk_prepare_enable fails with only a warning), sets the MMC limits and capabilities, requests the 'rx' and 'tx' DMA channels, requests the IRQ with devm_request_irq, calls omap_hsmmc_reg_get, calls omap_hsmmc_configure_wake_irq (a failure only leaves MMC_CAP_SDIO_IRQ unset), and calls mmc_add_host. A failure of the DMA channel requests, the IRQ request, omap_hsmmc_reg_get or mmc_add_host returns that error through err_irq; a failure of device_create_file for the slot name (only done if the platform data has a name) returns through err_slot_name, which first calls mmc_remove_host. err_irq clears device wakeup, releases whichever DMA channels were obtained, drops autosuspend use, drops the runtime-PM reference with pm_runtime_put_sync, disables runtime PM and disables the debounce clock if there is one. On success it adds the debugfs entries, drops the runtime-PM reference with pm_runtime_put_autosuspend and returns 0 with the host added, both DMA channels held, the IRQ requested, runtime PM enabled and the debounce clock (if it was obtained and enabled) left enabled.
note: Reviewer right: host->dbclk is set to NULL when clk_prepare_enable fails (omap_hsmmc.c:1863-1866), so 'debounce clock left enabled if obtained' was too broad (only if it was obtained and the enable succeeded). The old prose also said the unwinding applied to 'failures after runtime PM was enabled' without saying that earlier failures return directly. omap_hsmmc_probe at 1761-1972 (name was right, slice cut the head).

name: sdhci_msm_probe
prose: Precondition: pdev is a platform device whose OF match data is non-NULL (var_info is dereferenced without a check) and which has the 'iface' and 'core' clocks, a 'pwr_irq' interrupt and (unless mci_removed) a second memory resource. Postcondition: it calls sdhci_pltfm_init and returns PTR_ERR on failure, then mmc_of_parse, sdhci_msm_gcc_reset and, if a 'bus' clock exists, clk_set_rate(INT_MAX) and clk_prepare_enable on it; failures of these four return immediately with no unwinding. From here on failures go to bus_clk_disable, which disables the bus clock if there is one and returns the error: a missing 'iface' or 'core' clock, a failure of dev_pm_opp_of_find_icc_paths or devm_pm_opp_set_clkname, an invalid OPP table (a -ENODEV 'no table' result is tolerated), and a failure of clk_bulk_prepare_enable for the iface, core, cal and sleep clocks (no bulk clock is enabled in that case, so none is disabled). A failed dev_pm_opp_set_rate and a missing 'xo' clock only log a warning. After the bulk clocks are enabled, failures go to clk_disable, which disables the bulk clocks and then the bus clock: a failure to map the core memory resource (when mci_removed is false), a failure of sdhci_msm_register_vreg, a negative platform_get_irq_byname for 'pwr_irq', and a failure of devm_request_threaded_irq. It then sets runtime PM active, enabled and with autosuspend, installs the signal-voltage-switch and tuning ops and calls sdhci_msm_cqe_add_host if the node has 'supports-cqe' or sdhci_add_host otherwise; if that fails it goes to the pm_runtime_disable label, which disables runtime PM, marks the device suspended, drops the no-idle reference and then runs the clk_disable and bus_clk_disable steps. On success it calls pm_runtime_put_autosuspend and returns 0 with the clocks enabled, the power IRQ requested and the host added.
note: Reviewer right: clk_bulk_prepare_enable failure and the OPP/icc failures jump to bus_clk_disable, which only disables the bus clock (sdhci-msm.c:2646-2649 and 2796-2798); the old prose said the bulk clocks were disabled for those. Slice cut the head: sdhci_msm_probe at 2535-2800 (name was right). Also: var_info is used without a NULL check (2567-2572).

name: sdhci_s3c_probe
prose: Precondition: pdev is a platform device with either platform data or a device-tree node. Postcondition: it returns -ENOENT if neither is present, the negative platform_get_irq result, PTR_ERR of sdhci_alloc_host on failure, -ENOMEM if the platform data allocation fails, the error of sdhci_s3c_parse_dt (DT case) or copies the platform data, and returns PTR_ERR of the 'hsmmc' io clock if it cannot be obtained; each of these returns directly. Note that none of the error returns after sdhci_alloc_host calls sdhci_free_host, and platform_set_drvdata has already been done before the clock lookup. It then enables the io clock with clk_prepare_enable (the result is ignored) and looks for up to MAX_BUS_CLK clocks named mmc_busclk.N, recording their rates; if none is found it returns -ENOENT after disabling and unpreparing the io clock (err_no_busclks). It maps register resource 0 with devm_platform_ioremap_resource; if that fails it jumps to err_req_regs, which calls pm_runtime_disable even though pm_runtime_enable has not been called yet on this path, and then disables the io clock, returning the error. Otherwise it fills in the host quirks, ops, capabilities and pm caps from the driver and platform data, enables runtime PM with a 50 ms autosuspend, and calls mmc_of_parse and sdhci_add_host; a failure of either goes to err_req_regs (runtime PM disabled, io clock disabled) and returns the error. On success, if CONFIG_PM is set and pdata->cd_type is not S3C_SDHCI_CD_INTERNAL it disables and unprepares the io clock, otherwise leaves it enabled, and returns 0 with the host added.
note: Reviewer right: the ioremap failure goes to err_req_regs (sdhci-s3c.c:560-563 and 655-656), so pm_runtime_disable runs before pm_runtime_enable (636); the old prose said it was called 'only where runtime PM was already enabled'. Also noted: sdhci_alloc_host is never matched by sdhci_free_host on the error returns. sdhci_s3c_probe at 484-662 (name was right).

name: sdhci_setup_host
prose: Precondition: host points to an sdhci_host whose mmc pointer, ops, version, caps, caps1, quirks, quirks2 and v4_mode fields have been set by the caller, who keeps ownership. Postcondition: this is sdhci_setup_host. It returns -EINVAL (after WARN_ON) if host is NULL. If mmc->supply.vqmmc is not yet set it calls mmc_regulator_get_supply and returns its error if non-zero. It then selects DMA: if external DMA is requested and sdhci_external_dma_init returns -EPROBE_DEFER it goes to the unreg exit and returns -EPROBE_DEFER; any other external DMA error just switches back to the internal DMA/PIO. If SDMA or ADMA is enabled it calls the set_dma_mask (or sdhci_set_dma_mask) and enable_dma callbacks; a failure of those is not an error, it logs and falls back to PIO (flags cleared, ret reset to 0). With ADMA still enabled it allocates the coherent descriptor/alignment buffer; failure or misalignment only clears ADMA (the buffer is freed in the misaligned case), it does not fail. Only when neither SDMA nor ADMA remains does it set host->dma_mask to DMA_BIT_MASK(64) and point mmc_dev(mmc)->dma_mask at it; when DMA is used the caller is responsible for the mask. It then derives host->max_clk (from caps, or from ops->get_max_clock; if neither gives a base clock it returns -ENODEV through undma), clk_mul, mmc->f_min and f_max, the timeout clock (from caps, or ops->get_timeout_clock; if neither gives one it returns -ENODEV through undma) and the other capability, OCR, voltage and block size/count fields; it enables the vqmmc regulator when it obtained it here (a failed enable only warns and replaces the vqmmc pointer with an error pointer) and returns -ENODEV through unreg if the resulting mmc->ocr_avail is 0. Both exits undo only what was set up: unreg disables the vqmmc regulator if sdhci_core_to_disable_vqmmc is set and then falls into undma, which frees the coherent ADMA/alignment buffer if one was allocated and clears adma_table and align_buffer. On success it returns 0 (after possibly allocating a bounce buffer when max_segs is 1).
note: Reviewer right: host->dma_mask is assigned only in the PIO-only case (sdhci.c lines near 4437-4441), not when DMA is used. Old prose also described vqmmc/ADMA allocation failures loosely. Large function (sdhci.c:4283-4851, ~570 lines): I read the head, the DMA/clock/timeout sections, the vqmmc and ocr checks and the exit labels and grepped every return/goto, but not every capability and quirk assignment in the remainder, so the prose stays at the level of the returns and the state it provably sets. Read partly.

name: get_chip
prose: Precondition: the caller holds chip->mutex and passes a chip of map with an address adr and a valid FL_* mode. Postcondition: this is get_chip. If chip->priv is set (a hardware partition sharing a write/erase engine), mode is FL_WRITING, FL_ERASING, FL_OTP_WRITE or FL_SHUTDOWN and chip->state is not FL_SYNCING, it takes shared->lock and, if another partition (the contender) owns shared->writing, takes the contender's mutex with mutex_trylock (a lost race releases shared->lock and retries from the top), drops chip->mutex and calls chip_ready on the contender, retaking chip->mutex afterwards: a result of -EAGAIN releases the contender's mutex and retries; any other non-zero result releases the contender's mutex and is returned (with chip->mutex held and shared->lock not held); on success it retakes shared->lock and, if chip->state has become FL_SYNCING, calls put_chip on the contender, releases the contender's mutex and retries with shared->lock still held (and put_chip itself takes shared->lock when the contender has chip->priv, which this function holds at that point); otherwise it releases the contender's mutex. For FL_ERASING, if an erase is already suspended on the shared engine (shared->erasing->oldstate == FL_ERASING) it releases shared->lock, sleeps on chip->wq with chip->mutex dropped and retakes it, and retries. Otherwise it records ownership (shared->writing = chip, and shared->erasing = chip for FL_ERASING) and releases shared->lock. In all modes it finally calls chip_ready(map, chip, adr, mode): -EAGAIN retries from the top, and any other result, 0 or a negative error (for example -EIO), is returned; on a failing chip_ready the shared ownership recorded just before is not undone here. On return the caller again holds chip->mutex (it may have been released and retaken in between); the function never returns -EAGAIN itself.
note: Reviewer 1 right (a lost mutex_trylock race goes to retry, cfi_cmdset_0001.c:964-967, not -EAGAIN); reviewers 2 and 3 right (the FL_SYNCING path retries with shared->lock still held and without setting shared->writing, 982-987; the old prose claimed all locks were released and the postcondition set shared->writing on success). get_chip at 944-1020; put_chip at 1022 for the shared->lock observation.

name: cfi_amdstd_otp_walk
prose: Precondition: mtd is an AMD/Fujitsu-style CFI MTD whose private data are the map_info and cfi_private; retlen is writable; action is NULL (report otp_info records) or an otp_op_t callback; when action is NULL, buf must be writable for the records that will be emitted, and when action is non-NULL buf is only passed to action and so may be NULL if action accepts that. Postcondition: this is cfi_amdstd_otp_walk. It sets *retlen to 0 and walks all chips. Only Micron M29EW chips (is_m29ew) have OTP regions here: for such a chip it enters query mode under chip->mutex (get_chip with FL_CFI_QUERY; a failure releases the mutex and returns its error) to read whether the secsi area is factory locked (then a 0x100-byte factory region) or user lockable (then a 0x100-byte user region, whose lock bit it reads through the lock-register command sequence under get_chip with FL_LOCKING; a failure returns its error with the mutex released). For other chips, and for the region kind not selected by user_regs, the region size is 0 and the chip is skipped. For a selected region: if action is NULL it subtracts sizeof(struct otp_info) from the unsigned len and returns -ENOSPC if the result is exactly 0 (a len smaller than sizeof(struct otp_info) wraps around and is not rejected), otherwise it writes an otp_info record (start = from, length = region size, locked) at buf, advances buf and *retlen by sizeof(struct otp_info) and advances from by the region size; if action is non-NULL and from is within the region and len > 0 it calls action on min(len, region size - from) bytes at the region offset plus from, returns a negative result at once, otherwise advances buf, reduces len, adds the size to *retlen and sets from to 0; if from is beyond the region it just reduces from by the region size. After all chips it returns 0. On an error return *retlen holds only what was processed before the error. chip->mutex is taken and released around each chip access and no lock is held on return.
note: Prose was mostly right; the missing piece was that only M29EW chips yield any OTP region (cfi_cmdset_0002.c:1505-1558 and 1560-1562, otherwise otpsize is 0 and the chip is skipped), so for other chips the walk returns 0 with *retlen 0. Reviewer 2 right (-ENOSPC needs len exactly 0 after the subtraction since len is size_t, 1569-1571; wrap-around is not rejected). cfi_amdstd_otp_walk at 1480-1596; the prose's earlier description of -ENOSPC was already correct.

name: do_ppb_xxlock
prose: Precondition: thunk is DO_XXLOCK_ONEBLOCK_LOCK, DO_XXLOCK_ONEBLOCK_UNLOCK or DO_XXLOCK_ONEBLOCK_GETLOCK (any other value reaches BUG(), after the PPB entry commands have been sent), and the caller does not hold chip->mutex (the function takes and releases it). Postcondition: it adds chip->start to adr, takes chip->mutex and calls get_chip with FL_LOCKING; if that fails it releases the mutex and returns its error, having issued no command and not touched chip->state. Otherwise it sends the unlock-cycle commands and the PPB entry command 0xC0. For LOCK it sets chip->state to FL_LOCKING and writes 0xA0, 0x00 at adr; for UNLOCK it sets FL_UNLOCKING and writes 0x80, 0x30 at chip->start (all sectors of the chip are unlocked, not just one); for GETLOCK it sets FL_JEDEC_QUERY and sets the result to !cfi_read_query(map, adr), i.e. 1 if the value read at adr is 0 and 0 otherwise (the source comment says 0 means locked and 1 unlocked). It then polls chip_ready for up to 2 seconds with 1 us delays, and on timeout logs and sets the result to -EIO (overwriting a GETLOCK result). It then exits PPB command mode (writes 0x90 and 0x00), sets chip->state to FL_READY, calls put_chip, releases chip->mutex and returns the result: 0 for LOCK/UNLOCK on success, the 0/1 value for GETLOCK on success, or -EIO on timeout.
note: Reviewer 1 right (get_chip failure returns without setting FL_READY, cfi_cmdset_0002.c:2726-2730); reviewers 2 and 3 contradict each other on the GETLOCK polarity; the code is ret = !cfi_read_query(map, adr) (2757) with a comment '0->locked, 1->unlocked', so I state the literal code behaviour (1 when the query value is 0, else 0) rather than choosing a meaning. Also added: UNLOCK unlocks every sector of the chip, a timeout overrides the GETLOCK result with -EIO. do_ppb_xxlock at 2716-2787.

name: get_chip
prose: Precondition: the caller holds chip->mutex and passes a valid map, chip and operation mode. Postcondition: this is the lpddr get_chip. If chip->priv is set, mode is FL_WRITING or FL_ERASING and chip->state is not FL_SYNCING, it arbitrates the shared write/erase engine as in the CFI version: with shared->lock taken, if another partition owns shared->writing it trylocks that contender (a lost race retries), drops chip->mutex, calls chip_ready on the contender and retakes chip->mutex; -EAGAIN retries and any other non-zero result is returned after releasing the contender's mutex (so no ownership was recorded yet); on success, if chip->state has become FL_SYNCING it calls put_chip on the contender and retries with shared->lock still held (and put_chip takes shared->lock itself when chip->priv is set). For FL_ERASING with an erase already suspended on the engine it sleeps on chip->wq with chip->mutex dropped and retries. Otherwise it sets shared->writing to chip (and shared->erasing to chip for FL_ERASING) and releases shared->lock. In every case it finally calls chip_ready(map, chip, mode): -EAGAIN retries and any other result is returned; the ownership recorded just before is not undone if that call fails, so a returned -EIO from this last call does not mean no shared ownership was taken. chip_ready may suspend an erase (setting oldstate FL_ERASING, erase_suspended and state FL_READY), so on a 0 return chip->state is whatever chip_ready left, not necessarily the requested mode. The caller holds chip->mutex again on return (it may have been released and retaken); the function never returns -EAGAIN.
note: Reviewer 4 right: the shared ownership (shared->writing, shared->erasing) is recorded at lpddr_cmds.c:281-284 before the final chip_ready at 287, so a failure of that call returns an error with ownership taken; the old prose said no ownership on -EIO (true only for a failed contender chip_ready). Reviewers 2 and 3 also right (state left as chip_ready sets it). lpddr_cmds.c get_chip at 198-292 (chip_ready at 296-345).

name: mtdpstore_is_io_error
prose: Precondition: none; ret may be any int. Postcondition: it returns true exactly when ret is negative and is neither -EUCLEAN (mtd_is_bitflip, -117) nor -EBADMSG (mtd_is_eccerr, -74), and false otherwise (for ret == 0, ret == -117, ret == -74 and every positive value). It reads no state, takes no locks and allocates nothing.
contract: /*@ requires 	rue; ensures (ret < 0 && ret != -117 && ret != -74) ? result == 1 : result == 0; */
note: Matches mtdpstore_is_io_error (mtdpstore.c:301-304: ret < 0 && !mtd_is_bitflip(ret) && !mtd_is_eccerr(ret)). The repeated 'still-rejected' reasons were mechanical complaints about earlier contracts; the contract is rewritten with the explicit constants (-EUCLEAN = -117, -EBADMSG = -74 on Linux).

name: mtdpstore_flush_removed_do
prose: Precondition: cxt points to a valid mtdpstore_context whose cxt->mtd is an initialised MTD device, off is the start of an erase block (the function reads and erases mtd->erasesize bytes at off, whatever size is), and cxt->info.kmsg_size is non-zero (the loop advances off by it); no other precondition is checked. Postcondition: the function always frees its temporary buffer before returning; it returns -ENOMEM if the kmalloc of an erasesize buffer fails; otherwise it reads mtd->erasesize bytes at off into the buffer and, if that read fails with an I/O error (negative and neither -EUCLEAN nor -EBADMSG), returns that mtd_read error code, while a bitflip/ECC or non-negative read result is ignored and processing continues; then it erases the block at off and, if mtd_erase fails, returns the erase error code; then, while size is nonzero, for each zone of cxt->info.kmsg_size bytes starting at the current off, if the zone is marked used it writes the first zonesize bytes of the cached buffer to that zone (the same start-of-block data is written for every used zone, not per-zone data), continuing the loop even after a failed write, and advances off by zonesize and reduces size by min(zonesize, size); it returns the value of the last mtd_write attempted (0 if that write succeeded, its error code if it failed), or 0 if no write was attempted (e.g. size == 0 or no used zone); the caller retains ownership of cxt and nothing new is leaked.
note: Reviewer 2 right (the return value is the last mtd_write result, so an earlier write failure is lost if a later write succeeds, mtdpstore.c:478-486, 490); reviewer 3 right (the read and erase cover a whole erase block at off independent of size); reviewer 1 right (every used zone gets the data from the start of the buffer, 478, and success returns 0). Old prose already stated the writes-from-buffer-start and last-write semantics; I only tightened the precondition. mtdpstore_flush_removed_do at 447-491.

name: anfc_calc_hw_ecc_bytes
prose: Precondition: either step_size is neither 512 nor 1024 (strength may be any int), or step_size is 512 and strength is in [0, 330382099], or step_size is 1024 and strength is in [0, 306783377]. Postcondition: if step_size is neither 512 nor 1024 the function returns -EINVAL (-22); if step_size is 512 it returns ceil((13 * strength) / 8); if step_size is 1024 it returns ceil((14 * strength) / 8); no resources are acquired and the parameters are unmodified.
contract: /*@ requires ((step_size != 512 && step_size != 1024) || (step_size == 512 && strength >= 0 && strength <= 330382099) || (step_size == 1024 && strength >= 0 && strength <= 306783377)); ensures ((step_size != 512 && step_size != 1024) ==> result == -22) && (step_size == 512 ==> result == (13 * strength + 7) / 8) && (step_size == 1024 ==> result == (14 * strength + 7) / 8); */
note: Verified against arasan-nand-controller.c:1064-1082: SZ_512 gives bch_gf_mag 13, SZ_1K gives 14, anything else -EINVAL; result DIV_ROUND_UP(bch_gf_mag * strength, 8) in unsigned arithmetic. The strength bounds are exactly where 13 * s + 7 and 14 * s + 7 still fit in 32 bits (330382099 and 306783377), so prose and contract are correct as written (the contract already contains the -22 result). The earlier 'still-rejected' reasons were mechanical and refer to older contract versions.

name: calc_tdvw_max
prose: Precondition: with eff = clk_period / 2 when ext_mode == 0 and eff = clk_period otherwise, the mathematical value (trp_cnt + 1) * eff + trhoh_min + board_delay_skew_min is at most 4294967295, so no u32 operation wraps (this also excludes trp_cnt = 4294967295 with a non-zero eff). Postcondition: it returns exactly (trp_cnt + 1) * eff + trhoh_min + board_delay_skew_min as a u32. It halves only its own local copy of clk_period; the caller's value is unchanged. It reads no state, takes no locks and allocates nothing.
contract: /*@ requires (trp_cnt + 1) * (ext_mode == 0 ? clk_period / 2 : clk_period) + trhoh_min + board_delay_skew_min <= 4294967295; ensures result == (trp_cnt + 1) * (ext_mode == 0 ? clk_period / 2 : clk_period) + trhoh_min + board_delay_skew_min; */
note: Matches calc_tdvw_max (cadence-nand-controller.c:2328-2336). The old contract's postcondition used the unhalved clk_period (so it was false when ext_mode == 0, as the random tests found); the corrected contract uses the same effective period as the precondition.

name: calc_tdvw
prose: Precondition: with eff = clk_period / 2 when ext_mode == 0 and eff = clk_period otherwise, the mathematical value (trp_cnt + 1) * eff + trhoh_min is at least trea_max and at most 4294967295, so no u32 operation wraps. Postcondition: it returns exactly (trp_cnt + 1) * eff + trhoh_min - trea_max as a u32. It halves only its own local copy of clk_period; the caller's value is unchanged. It reads no state, takes no locks and allocates nothing.
contract: /*@ requires (trp_cnt + 1) * (ext_mode == 0 ? clk_period / 2 : clk_period) + trhoh_min >= trea_max && (trp_cnt + 1) * (ext_mode == 0 ? clk_period / 2 : clk_period) + trhoh_min <= 4294967295; ensures result == (trp_cnt + 1) * (ext_mode == 0 ? clk_period / 2 : clk_period) + trhoh_min - trea_max; */
note: Matches calc_tdvw (cadence-nand-controller.c:2339-2346). As for calc_tdvw_max, the old postcondition used the unhalved clk_period and was false for ext_mode == 0.

name: loongson_nand_is_valid_cmd_seq
prose: Precondition: opcode1 and opcode2 are the two command opcodes of the sequence being checked, each a byte value in 0..255. Postcondition: the function returns 0 exactly when the pair is (NAND_CMD_RNDOUT=0x05, NAND_CMD_RNDOUTSTART=0xe0), (NAND_CMD_READ0=0x00, NAND_CMD_READSTART=0x30), (NAND_CMD_ERASE1=0x60, NAND_CMD_ERASE2=0xd0) or (NAND_CMD_SEQIN=0x80, NAND_CMD_PAGEPROG=0x10), and returns -EOPNOTSUPP (-95) for every other pair; it allocates no memory and takes no locks.
contract: /*@ requires 0 <= opcode1 <= 255 && 0 <= opcode2 <= 255; ensures (result == 0) <==> ((opcode1 == 0x05 && opcode2 == 0xe0) || (opcode1 == 0x00 && opcode2 == 0x30) || (opcode1 == 0x60 && opcode2 == 0xd0) || (opcode1 == 0x80 && opcode2 == 0x10)); ensures (result == -95) <==> !((opcode1 == 0x05 && opcode2 == 0xe0) || (opcode1 == 0x00 && opcode2 == 0x30) || (opcode1 == 0x60 && opcode2 == 0xd0) || (opcode1 == 0x80 && opcode2 == 0x10)); */
note: Verified against loongson-nand-controller.c:606-621 (four accepted pairs, otherwise -EOPNOTSUPP = -95; NAND_CMD_RNDOUT 0x05, RNDOUTSTART 0xe0, READ0 0x00, READSTART 0x30, ERASE1 0x60, ERASE2 0xd0, SEQIN 0x80, PAGEPROG 0x10). Prose and contract unchanged; the earlier rejections were mechanical complaints about older contract versions.

name: nand_detect
prose: Precondition: chip is a valid nand_chip whose mtd is attached, and type is NULL (the built-in nand_flash_ids table is then used) or a valid flash-ID table. Postcondition: this is nand_detect. It sets memorg planes_per_lun and luns_per_target to 1, resets the chip with nand_reset (error returned), selects target 0 and reads the first two ID bytes and then the full ID with nand_readid_op (a failure is returned); if the second read's first two bytes differ from the first it returns -ENODEV. It sets chip->id.len and chip->manufacturer.desc, saves the configured NAND_BUSWIDTH_16 option and clears it, and searches the table for a full-ID or device-ID match. If there is no match or the match has no page size it tries nand_onfi_detect and then nand_jedec_detect (a negative result from either is returned at once; a positive result skips the table decoding); if the table has no matching entry and neither ONFI nor JEDEC identified the chip it returns -ENODEV. For a table match it duplicates the model name into chip->parameters.model (-ENOMEM on failure, which the caller must free on success), decodes the ID or asks the manufacturer code, ORs in type->options and sets memorg->eraseblocks_per_lun. At ident_done it sets mtd->name to the model if mtd->name was NULL. If NAND_BUSWIDTH_AUTO is set it applies nand_set_defaults; otherwise, if the detected bus width differs from the saved one, it logs and returns -EINVAL after freeing chip->parameters.model (without clearing the pointer or mtd->name). For a bus-width match, or with auto width, it then fills chip->page_shift, pagemask, chip_shift, phys_erase_shift and bbt_erase_shift, may set NAND_ROW_ADDR_3, sets badblockbits to 8, adjusts the legacy command functions, logs the device and returns 0. Nothing is deselected or unlocked at the end.
note: Reviewer right: the -EINVAL bus-width check is in the 'else if' after the NAND_BUSWIDTH_AUTO test (nand_base.c:5251-5268), so it does not apply when auto width is set; the old prose omitted that exception. Slice cut the head: nand_detect at 5120-5307 (name was right). Extra: on the -EINVAL path mtd->name may still point at the freed model string (5248-5249, 5303-5304).

name: write_bbt
prose: Precondition: this, td and md are valid nand_chip and bad block table descriptors; chipsel is -1 or a valid chip (target) index (it only matters with NAND_BBT_PERCHIP); buf is large enough for the mode used: with NAND_BBT_SAVECONTENT a whole erase block (1 << bbt_erase_shift bytes) followed by the OOB data of all its pages, and otherwise the page-aligned table length plus (that length >> page_shift) * oobsize bytes of OOB (or just the aligned length with NAND_BBT_NO_OOB). Postcondition: this is write_bbt. It processes the chips from chipsel (or from 0 when chipsel is -1 or the table is not per chip) to the last one. For each chip it asks get_bbt_block for a block; if that is negative it logs and returns that negative value. It then derives the bit width from td->options & NAND_BBT_NRBITS_MSK and returns -EINVAL for any value other than 1, 2, 4 or 8. With NAND_BBT_SAVECONTENT it reads the whole block with mtd_read (a negative result with a short read length is returned at once; an ECC error with a full-length read is only warned about) and the OOB with mtd_read_oob (a negative result or a short OOB length returns the value of res, which can be 0 if only the length was short); otherwise it just prepares an 0xff-filled buffer with the pattern. It fills the table bits from the in-memory table, erases the block with nand_erase_nand and writes it with scan_write_bbt; if the erase or the write fails it marks that block bad with mark_bbt_block_bad and repeats the same chip with a new block instead of returning. On success of both it stores the page number in td->pages[chip] and moves to the next chip. It returns 0 after the last chip.
note: Reviewer right: with NAND_BBT_SAVECONTENT the function reads a full erase block plus its OOB into buf (nand_bbt.c:821-838), so the old precondition on buf was too weak. Rest of the old prose verified against write_bbt at 744-920 (returns, the outerr path returning res which may be 0 for a short OOB read, erase/write failures retrying the chip).

name: nand_onfi_detect
prose: Precondition: chip is a valid nand_chip whose target is selected and whose controller operations work; this is nand_onfi_detect(chip) (the packet slice starts in its middle). Postcondition: it reads 4 bytes at address 0x20 with nand_readid_op and returns 0 (not an ONFI chip) if that fails or the bytes are not 'ONFI'. Otherwise it allocates a buffer for ONFI_PARAM_PAGES copies of the parameter page (-ENOMEM on failure) and reads the copies one by one with the read-parameter-page or data-in or change-column operation: a read failure ends detection with a return of 0; the first copy whose CRC matches is used. If none matches it recovers a page by bit-wise majority and returns 0 if the CRC of the result is still wrong. It applies the manufacturer's fixup_onfi_param_page hook if there is one, derives onfi_version from the revision field, and returns 0 (after logging) if no supported version bit is set. Otherwise it sanitises the manufacturer and model strings and duplicates the model into chip->parameters.model (-ENOMEM on failure), fills the memory organisation and mtd fields (page size, power-of-two truncated pages per block and blocks per LUN, OOB size, LUNs, planes, bits per cell, max bad blocks), sets NAND_BUSWIDTH_16 if the 16-bit feature is set, sets the ECC requirements (or tries the extended parameter page, whose failure only logs a warning, or warns that no ECC requirements were found), records the get/set-features and read-cache support, and allocates and fills chip->parameters.onfi (on a -ENOMEM there the model string is freed again, but the memory organisation and mtd fields set earlier stay modified). On success it frees the parameter page buffer and returns 1. The parameter page buffer is freed on every path.
note: Slice cut the head and the packet name was wrong: the function is nand_onfi_detect(chip) (nand_onfi.c:167-~343), not nand_flash_detect_onfi_param_page(chip, p, ...); the old prose invented parameters 'p' and 'onfi_version'. The old return summary (0 for unsupported version, 1 on success, -ENOMEM) was right as far as it went but missed the other 0 returns (not ONFI, read failures, unrecoverable CRC) and the buffer allocation. Mechanical reviewer right on the name.

name: skyhigh_spinand_ecc_get_status
prose: Precondition: spinand is a valid SPI NAND device (it is not used) and status is the status byte read from it. Postcondition: the ECC status field is status & STATUS_ECC_MASK, where STATUS_ECC_MASK = GENMASK(5, 4) = 0x30. It returns 0 when the field is 0x00 (no bitflips), -EBADMSG (-74) when it is 0x30 (uncorrectable), 2 when it is 0x10 (1 to 2 bitflips) and 6 when it is 0x20 (3 to 6 bitflips). The remaining return, -EINVAL (-22) for any other field value, cannot be reached because the masked field only takes those four values. It takes no locks and allocates nothing.
contract: /*@ requires 	rue; ensures (((status & 0x30) == 0x00) ==> result == 0) && (((status & 0x30) == 0x10) ==> result == 2) && (((status & 0x30) == 0x20) ==> result == 6) && (((status & 0x30) == 0x30) ==> result == -74); */
note: Old prose and contract used the mask 0x70, but STATUS_ECC_MASK is GENMASK(5, 4) = 0x30 (include/linux/mtd/spinand.h:262), so bit 6 is not part of the field; with the correct mask all four field values are handled and the -EINVAL default (skyhigh.c:76-80) is unreachable. skyhigh_spinand_ecc_get_status at 60-81. The earlier 'still-rejected' reasons were mechanical.

name: NFTL_foldchain
prose: Precondition: nftl is a valid NFTL record whose EUNtable and ReplUnitTable describe the chain of virtual unit thisVUC; pendingblock is the block number of a pending write (it may lie outside this chain). Postcondition: this is NFTL_foldchain. It returns BLOCK_NIL, with no table changed by this function, if EUNtable[thisVUC] is BLOCK_NIL (logged), if the scan of the chain runs more than MAX_LOOPS steps (logged as an infinite loop), or if fold-out-of-place is needed and NFTL_findfreeblock(nftl, 1) returns BLOCK_NIL. Otherwise it scans every unit of the chain reading the OOB of each 512-byte block to build a map of which unit holds the live data of each block, decides whether it can fold in place into the last unit of the chain (not if a fold is marked in progress, if some live block is not in that unit and its slot there is not free, or if the pending block's slot is not free) or must find a free unit with NFTL_findfreeblock; for an in-place fold it first writes a FOLD_MARK_IN_PROGRESS mark to the target unit's OOB. It then copies each live block that is not already in the target unit and is not the pending block with NFTL_move_block, writes the target unit's header with the virtual unit number and no replacement unit, formats every other unit of the old chain with NFTL_formatblock and marks it BLOCK_FREE in ReplUnitTable (incrementing nftl->numfreeEUNs) or BLOCK_RESERVED if the erase fails, sets ReplUnitTable[targetEUN] to BLOCK_NIL and EUNtable[thisVUC] to targetEUN, and returns targetEUN. The results of the block moves and of the OOB writes are not checked.
note: Slice cut the head and the packet name was wrong: the function is NFTL_foldchain (nftlcore.c:250-~468), not NFTL_fold. Old prose was mostly right; changes: 'without changing the tables' is stated only for this function's own table updates (NFTL_findfreeblock is a callee), the in-place decision rules and the fold mark are described, and the unchecked move/OOB-write results are noted. Mechanical reviewer right on the name.

name: bcm4908_partitions_fw_offset
prose: Precondition: none; it reads the device tree. It takes a reference on the root device node with of_find_node_by_path and releases it with of_node_put on every path after taking it. Postcondition: it returns -ENOENT (-2) if there is no root node, or if no string of the root's brcm_blparms property has the form BLPARAMS_FW_OFFSET followed by '='. For the first string that does have that form it parses the text after '=' with kstrtoul using base 0 (so hex and octal prefixes are accepted) and returns the negative kstrtoul error (-EINVAL or -ERANGE) if that fails, and otherwise returns the parsed value shifted left by 10 bits, converted from unsigned long to long long (a multiple of 1024; a very large value wraps and may convert to a negative number, which a caller would then see as an error code). The caller supplies and receives no reference.
note: Verified against ofpart_bcm4908.c:17-48. The earlier 'still-rejected' reasons were mechanical about the formal contract omitting the error returns; I removed the contract (rule 4: the function reads global device-tree state). Added: kstrtoul base 0, first matching entry decides, and the possible negative result after wrap-around.

name: spi_nor_hwcaps_read2cmd
prose: Precondition: hwcaps is any 32-bit value. Postcondition: it looks hwcaps up in a static 16-entry table of (SNOR_HWCAPS_READ* flag, SNOR_CMD_READ* index) pairs, comparing as int, and returns the index of the first entry whose flag equals hwcaps. Because the flags are BIT(0) to BIT(15) in the same order as the SNOR_CMD_READ enumerators (READ = 0, READ_FAST = 1, READ_1_1_1_DTR = 2, ..., READ_8_8_8_DTR = 15), this is the position of the single set bit (0 to 15) when hwcaps is exactly one of the sixteen read flags 1, 2, 4, ..., 32768; for every other value, including 0, multi-bit masks and anything with a bit above 15, it returns -EINVAL (-22). It reads no state, takes no locks and allocates nothing.

name: cypress_nor_set_addr_mode_nbytes
prose: Precondition: nor points to an initialised SPI NOR flash with valid params and bouncebuf, supporting write enable/disable, the any-register read and the 4-byte address mode switch. Postcondition: it calls spi_nor_write_enable and returns its error if non-zero. It then determines the current address mode from SR1 (cypress_nor_determine_addr_mode_by_sr1). If that detection fails it calls spi_nor_set_4byte_addr_mode(nor, true) and returns its error if non-zero, and otherwise returns the result of spi_nor_write_disable (0 or an error), without updating either params field. If detection succeeds it calls spi_nor_write_disable (error returned), reads CFR2V with spi_nor_read_any_reg using the detected address width (error returned), and if the ADRBYT bit of CFR2V disagrees with the detected mode (ADRBYT set but mode not 4, or clear but mode not 3) it returns the result of spi_nor_set_4byte_addr_mode(nor, true), which is 0 or an error, again without updating either params field. Only when everything agrees does it set nor->params->addr_nbytes and nor->params->addr_mode_nbytes to the detected 3 or 4 and return 0.
note: Reviewer 3 right (the detection-failure branch returns the error of spi_nor_set_4byte_addr_mode if that fails, before the write-disable result, spansion.c:457-461); reviewer 2 right (it returns write_disable's result when the forcing succeeds); reviewer 1 right (the forced 4-byte paths return 0 without setting the params fields, 458-461 and 478-484). cypress_nor_set_addr_mode_nbytes at 443-490.

name: self_check_ai
prose: Precondition: ubi is an initialised UBI device and ai is the attach information built by scanning it (ai->vidb valid, volumes tree and the free, corr, erase and alien lists populated); the caller owns both and the function modifies neither. Postcondition: this is self_check_ai. It returns 0 at once, checking nothing, if general self-checks are disabled (ubi_dbg_chk_gen(ubi) is false). Otherwise it first checks the in-memory information for every volume and LEB record (the is_empty flag, non-negative values, volume id and type ranges, data_pad, erase counters against ai->min_ec and ai->max_ec, PEB numbers below peb_count, used_ebs and lnum rules, highest_lnum and leb_count, and that ai->vols_found matches the number of volumes) and then reads the VID header of every referenced PEB with ubi_io_read_vid_hdr and compares vol_type, sqnum, vol_id, compat, lnum, used_ebs and data_pad, and for the last LEB of each volume also highest_lnum and last_data_size. Any failed consistency check logs, dumps the volume, LEB or VID header, calls dump_stack and returns -EINVAL. A VID header read that fails with an error other than UBI_IO_BITFLIPS is logged and returns that error (a positive one converted to -EIO), without the stack dump. Finally it allocates a one-byte-per-PEB map (-ENOMEM on failure), marks bad PEBs (a negative result of ubi_io_is_bad frees the map and is returned) and every PEB found in a volume tree or in the free, corr, erase or alien list, and returns -EINVAL after dumping a stack if some PEB is referenced nowhere; the map is freed on every path that allocated it. Otherwise it returns 0.
note: Not a bare 'ubi_check_all_pebs' excerpt: the slice 1815-1925 is inside self_check_ai (ubi/attach.c:1660-~1900); the packet name was invented. Old prose said -EINVAL for a VID header read failure; the code returns the read error itself (or -EIO) at ubi/attach.c about line 1773-1778 of the function body, without dump_stack, and the old text did not mention that the whole check is skipped when ubi_dbg_chk_gen is off. Mechanical reviewer right on the name.
